codeReview.summary: The calendar skill implementation in commit 3bc3074 is comprehensive and well-structured. All 6 required actions (create_task, list_tasks, update_task, complete_task, overdue_check, set_reminder) are correctly implemented in handler.py with proper input validation, async DB operations, and error handling. The manifest.yaml fully defines all parameters with enums. Two SQLAlchemy models (TaskCalendar, TaskReminder) are added to core/database.py with appropriate indexes. 38 tests in test_calendar.py cover all actions including success paths, error handling, edge cases, and registry integration. The skill correctly declares no permissions (no shell/network needed) and category 'productivity'. NOTE: The handoff from session f8e02774 describes implementing backup_automation (commit 7bf5d52), not calendar. The actual calendar implementation is in commit 3bc3074 which appears to have been done separately — the handoff/session mapping is incorrect, but the code deliverable is correct and complete.

issues.description: Invalid reminder timestamps in the 'reminders' array for create_task are silently skipped (pass in except block). Users receive no feedback about which reminders failed to parse. Consider appending warnings to the output or returning a 'skipped_reminders' count in the data dict.

Invalid date_from/date_to filters in list_tasks are silently ignored (pass in except blocks at lines 180 and 186). This could confuse users who provide a malformed date — they'd get unfiltered results without knowing their filter was dropped. Consider returning an error or a warning.

TaskReminder.task_id has no ForeignKey constraint to tasks_calendar.id. However, this is consistent with the project-wide pattern — no other model in database.py uses ForeignKey constraints. The handler code does verify task existence before creating reminders, so this is acceptable but means orphan reminders could accumulate if tasks are deleted through other means.
Unused imports: 'text' from sqlalchemy and 'Any, Dict, List, Optional' from typing are imported but never used in the module. Minor code hygiene issue.
